The 3-group WHO classification (Group I / II / III) already encodes the communicable-vs-noncommunicable distinction (Group I = Communicable, Group II = Noncommunicable, Group III = Injuries); a separate binary column would be redundant.

decision_log.decision: Cause of Death names verbatim per WHO GHE 2021 workbook labels
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit's master dump: WHO uses specific cause labels that may differ from Wikipedia/colloquial usage. Examples: 'Alzheimer disease and other dementias' (NOT 'Alzheimer's disease' — WHO drops possessive per ICD convention); 'Trachea, bronchus, lung cancers' (compound-anatomy cancer label); 'Lower respiratory infections' (NOT 'Pneumonia' alone); 'Kidney diseases' (plural); 'Hypertensive heart disease' (distinct from Ischaemic heart disease). Verbatim preservation per audit's dump avoids ambiguity.

Per cycle-1 audit's verbatim dump format. WHO GHE workbook publishes death counts at thousand-precision (e.g., 9,033,116 deaths = 9.033116 million). 6-decimal precision in millions preserves WHO's published exactness while keeping cell values readable. Mirror precedent for 6-decimal precision: `top_15_most_produced_crops_by_global_production` (FAOSTAT production at 6-decimal millions of tonnes).

Verbose preservation maintains source-extractive integrity. Mirror precedent: `top_15_most_produced_crops_by_global_production` (FAOSTAT crop labels verbatim including parentheticals).

Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'Category top_k, operation_type=top_k.' top_k primary because the universe is a top-N ranking by Estimated Deaths DESC. set_filter secondary because the universe is set-filtered to top-15 + WHO GHE 2021 release scope. decision_log.decision: Entity class = abstract-categories/causes-of-death (NEW fine-class extending abstract-categories from 7 → 8)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'Entity class abstract-categories/causes-of-death is appropriate.' Causes of death are conceptual classifications (named medical-cause categories), NOT individual physical entities. Abstract-categories bucket matches the conceptual-classification framing — same precedent as `periodic_table_groups_first_three_elements_by_atomic_number` (abstract-categories/chemical-groups for IUPAC group classification). NEW fine-class extending abstract-categories bucket from 7 to 8 instances (joining music-genres, religions×2, languages, philosophical-schools, architectural-styles, chemical-groups).

Structural fix. operation_type was previously 'top_k', but top_k is NOT in OPERATION_TYPES; the canonical enum is {join, union, intersect, projection, union+filter, filter, aggregation} (curation_ui/app.py:60). An invalid value silently coerces to index-0 'join' if the instance is opened in the curation UI (app.py:1388-1391) and is flagged by validate_operation_query_pair (app.py:655-675). The earlier decision_log entry 'Category = top_k primary; secondary = set_filter' (citing a cycle-1 audit confirmation of 'operation_type=top_k') referenced a non-existent vocabulary value. For query_category=top_k, the contract-allowed operation_types are {projection, filter, union+filter}. Chose projection because the db_analog is a pure ranked column-selection: the top-15 cutoff is expressed via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY estimated_deaths_2021_millions DESC) + LIMIT 15 with NO WHERE predicate, and the outer SELECT just projects the four columns ordered by rank — the structural primitive is a multi-column SELECT (projection), not a filter. Verified projection ∈ validate_operation_query_pair allowed set for top_k = {projection, filter, union+filter}. No CSV rows, query_category (still top_k), secondary_category (still set_filter), primary_key, column_types, db_analog logic, source_count, or source_urls changed; only operation_type + this decision_log entry.

normalization_decisions.rule: WHO GHE 2021 workbook cause label verbatim (15 closed values per cycle-1 audit's dump). WHO conventions: 'Alzheimer disease and other dementias' (NOT 'Alzheimer's disease' — possessive dropped per ICD convention); 'Trachea, bronchus, lung cancers' (compound-anatomy plural; comma-separated organ list); 'Lower respiratory infections' (NOT 'Pneumonia' alone — broader category including bronchitis + bronchiolitis); 'Kidney diseases' (plural); 'Hypertensive heart disease' vs 'Ischaemic heart disease' (distinct WHO cause categories); 'Cirrhosis of the liver' (full anatomical specification); 'Colon and rectum cancers' (combined-organ cancer label); 'Diarrhoeal diseases' (British spelling 'Diarrhoeal' NOT 'Diarrheal' — WHO uses British English); 'Road injury' (singular — the only Group III: Injuries row in top-15).

Integer 1-15 ranked by Estimated Deaths 2021 DESC per WHO GHE 2021 workbook. Rank 1 = Ischaemic heart disease (9.033116 million deaths); Rank 15 = Colon and rectum cancers (0.954421 million deaths). No ties in the staged 15-row universe (rank 10 Tuberculosis 1.394973M vs rank 11 Hypertensive heart disease 1.386352M are close but distinct).

Numeric value at 6-decimal precision in millions per WHO GHE 2021 workbook. Examples: Ischaemic heart disease 9.033116 (= 9,033,116 deaths); COVID-19 8.721899; Colon and rectum cancers 0.954421 (= 954,421 deaths). 6-decimal precision preserves WHO's published thousand-level exactness. Source: WHO GHE 2021 'Global summary estimates' workbook.

Closed 3-value categorical per WHO classification: 'Group I: Communicable, maternal, perinatal and nutritional conditions' (4 rows: COVID-19 / Lower respiratory infections / Tuberculosis / Diarrhoeal diseases) / 'Group II: Noncommunicable diseases' (10 rows: Ischaemic HD / Stroke / COPD / Lung cancers / Alzheimer / Diabetes / Kidney / Hypertensive HD / Cirrhosis / Colon-rectum cancers) / 'Group III: Injuries' (1 row: Road injury). Verbose labels preserved per cycle-1 audit's dump. WHO's GHO interactive section uses shorter labels (Communicable / Noncommunicable / Injuries) but the GHE workbook uses the verbose forms.

open_questions.question: When WHO publishes 2022+ Global Health Estimates, should the instance be re-staged?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when WHO publishes a newer GHE release (typically every 2-3 years), the top-15 ranking may shift (rare for rank 1-3 to change; mid-pack rankings can move). Universe is locked to WHO GHE 2021 release as of cycle-0 staging date. temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this multi-year-update cadence.

open_questions.question: Why use WHO's verbose Group labels (e.g., 'Group I: Communicable, maternal, perinatal and nutritional conditions') instead of short labels (Communicable / Noncommunicable / Injuries)?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit's master dump — WHO GHE workbook uses the verbose forms. The GHO interactive section uses short labels for display but the underlying GHE workbook (the value source) uses verbose. Verbatim preservation per the source-extractive principle.

open_questions.question: Why is COVID-19 ranked #2 in 2021 but absent in pre-pandemic rankings?
open_questions.answer: WHO GHE 2021 captures pandemic-era mortality (COVID-19 emerged 2019, with peak global mortality 2020-2021). In WHO GHE 2019 (pre-pandemic), COVID-19 was not in the leading causes ranking. The 2021 ranking reflects pandemic-era mortality patterns; future GHE releases (2022+) may show COVID-19 dropping rank as pandemic wanes.

open_questions.question: Why 'Alzheimer disease' instead of 'Alzheimer's disease'?
open_questions.answer: Per WHO + ICD convention: medical cause names drop possessive apostrophe. WHO GHE 2021 workbook uses 'Alzheimer disease and other dementias' verbatim. This convention applies to other eponymous diseases too ('Parkinson disease' not 'Parkinson's', 'Down syndrome' not 'Down's' in modern usage).

open_questions.question: Should the schema include a 5th cell for ICD-11 chapter code?
open_questions.answer: No — per cycle-1 audit's required edit, 4-col schema is sufficient. ICD-11 chapter codes would be deeply technical (e.g., 'IX' for Diseases of the circulatory system); the WHO Cause Group 3-value categorical captures the same broad classification more readably.
